component.name: VeilVoice
component.summary: Destroy the voiceprint in a recording, keep the words

description.p: VeilVoice destroys the biometric voiceprint of a speaker: pitch, formants, timbre, micro-timing and the melody of an accent. Neither software nor a human listener can re-identify the speaker or reconstruct the original voice, while the words themselves stay clean and transcribable.

It does not hide what was said. Intelligibility is preserved on purpose, and the words remain in the output and can be transcribed. If the message itself is sensitive, encrypt it: that is a separate problem with a separate answer.

ul.li: Anonymise a recording, with metadata stripped, faster than real time
Scramble a microphone live, into a virtual audio cable
Encrypt recordings at rest by default, X25519 with ML-KEM-768
Strip audio tags, image EXIF and GPS
Report which applications are holding the microphone or camera
A strong regional accent may still be audible: what phonemes you produced cannot be changed at the signal level
The application lock is a verifier, not encryption, and is not tamper-proof
Secure erase is unreliable on flash storage

description.p: Fully offline by construction: there is no networking code, and this Flatpak requests no network permission.

A safety catch that notices when another program picks up a real microphone while you are being veiled, a baseline of what normally runs on the machine, a second passphrase that opens the application with nothing in it, and an interface that reads like English.
